output.summary: The ED length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (E5: about 3.0 of 3.2 hours). Boarding began in March, when the hospitalist rounding change moved discharges later on the medical wards (E6, E8, E9). Surgical wards, which were not changed, show no shift. A pilot with schedule-determined, comparable days cut boarding from 4.6 to 2.3 hours, and other wards were unaffected (E10, E11). ED nurse staffing hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance are flat, and volume, acuity and bed capacity are flat. So understaffing, volume and capacity are not the main cause. The ED nurses' workload and the front-end metrics reflect boarding. The evening cleaning cut is unmeasured. The travel nurse contract would defer case managers, and pausing the huddle would remove the one working fix. Extend the huddle.
